doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Hiring Charles Lloyd and Gabor Szabo
summary: He gave Charles Lloyd his first job after USC, when the alto player was unpopular, and Gabor Szabo introduced himself after hearing the group at Newport.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: Oh, it definitely does. Yeah, it’s just as fresh as the day you waxed it. I’m holding another one, Chico Hamilton, The Man From Two Worlds.
This introduces Forest Flower with Charles Lloyd.
How did you hook up with Charles Lloyd?
I gave Charles his first job man when he graduated from USC, you know.
No, he wasn’t the musician he was. He developed while he was with me. You know, he was just a young player. As a matter of fact, people hated him in the beginning.
They didn’t like the way he played. He played alto, you know, he was an alto player.
Yeah, after he got this tenor.
After he got this tenor, okay. So alto, he was not impressive?
What about the Gabor, how did you meet with him? He’s Hungarian, correct?

Gabor heard us at the Newport Jazz Festival and he loved the group, the sound, and he made it a point of introducing himself to me and when he came to California he made sure that I met him, you know, and one thing led to another. He and Charles hit it off, and Albert, so, you know, here again man, we happened to be four guys in the right place at the right time.
